environment.description: Same application deployed in a Podman container on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (oauth_consumer_t). The policy module was compiled with checkmodule and loaded via semodule. The type oauth_consumer_t is assigned to the container process via container_file_t transitions. The policy specifies: allow oauth_consumer_t oauth_token_store_t:file { read write create append getattr }; allow oauth_consumer_t oauth_token_store_t:dir { search add_name write }; with oauth_token_store_t labeled only on /var/lib/oauth/tokens/ (flat directory, no subdirectory traversal allowed via type_transition rules). All other file types including etc_t, cron_spool_t, tmp_t, and unlabeled_t have explicit dontaudit and neverallow rules against oauth_consumer_t. The container also runs with --security-opt no-new-privileges and the Podman seccomp profile blocks symlink/link syscalls. Network egress is restricted via nftables to port 443 toward the OAuth provider CIDR only.

config.selinux_policy_module: oauth_consumer_t with neverallow rules against etc_t, cron_spool_t, tmp_t, unlabeled_t
config.filesystem_labels: only /var/lib/oauth/tokens/ labeled oauth_token_store_t (flat, no subdir type_transition)
config.network_egress: nftables restricting outbound to OAuth provider CIDR on port 443 only
config.sqs_access: IAM role with condition key restricting SendMessage to internal service accounts only
